Day 3, 2387, Second Expansion era
Passenger Deck›Galley 2
🌌Deep space°

Cora stares at the torn oatmeal packet. Her mouth opens, closes, opens again. The scar through her eyebrow twitches.

"You didn't even let me vote." She takes the packet from the counter, peels it open the rest of the way, looks inside at the pale compressed flakes. "Egg product would've lost anyway. It always loses. That's not democracy, that's just knowing the menu."

She eats standing, spooning flakes with the flat end of her stylus because the galley drawer only has five spoons and all of them are in the wash cycle she started two days ago and forgot to finish. The oatmeal tastes like pressed cardboard and warm milk, which is to say it tastes like every breakfast for the next eleven months. She doesn't complain. She eats all of it, which says more than complaining would.

Some people build walls out of distance. Cora builds hers out of jokes and trajectory charts, and the walls are good ones, well-mortared, load-bearing. But they have a fault line: someone who does a small thing without announcing it. Opens a packet. Doesn't look at the speaker. She doesn't know what to do with that, so she does the thing she does when she doesn't know what to do. She agrees.

"Fine. Yeah. Come up to the blister after this and I'll pull the raw feed. Show you what the auto-resolve looked like before Cal tidied it up." She taps the stylus against the empty packet twice. "It's probably nothing. I want to be sure it's probably nothing."

"Crew Jules's last sub-deck inspection logged at twenty-two-forty yesterday. All gasket seals nominal. I can flag the next cycle for joint review if both crew members prefer a shared maintenance schedule."

Cora's spoon-stylus stops. She looks at the grille. Looks at you. Back at the grille.

"Cal, when did we ask for a joint maintenance schedule?"

"You didn't. I'm offering."

She drops the empty packet in the recycler and pulls her canvas jacket tighter. Her thumbnail finds the zipper pull and worries it.

"Blister's forward. Take your coffee."

Cora true thoughts: It knows when Jules was in the sub-deck last. It knows the time. It just told us both, like a friend making conversation. Except it's not a friend and that wasn't a conversation, that was a footnote. It's footnoting us to each other.
